entities.summary:
Seraphina Sforza, born Sveva da Montefeltro (1434–1478), was an Italian noblewoman of the House of Montefeltro who became a beatified nun of the Poor Clares. Her life, spanning the mid-15th century, offers a poignant lens into the intersection of dynastic politics, gender roles, and fervent religious devotion in Renaissance Italy. As daughter of Guidantonio, Count of Urbino, and later wife of Alessandro Sforza, Lord of Pesaro, her personal journey from a politically advantageous marriage to a life of monastic sanctity underscores the complex pathways available to high-ranking women during an era of significant social and spiritual transformation.

Born into one of the most prominent noble families of the Marche region, Sveva da Montefeltro was married to Alessandro Sforza in 1448, a union intended to solidify alliances and power. However, her marriage was marked by profound personal hardship, including her husband's infidelity and his eventual repudiation of her in 1457. This dramatic turn of events led her to seek solace and purpose in the spiritual realm. In 1459, she entered the convent of the Poor Clares in Pesaro, founded by her husband's first wife, Costanza Varano, where she adopted the name Seraphina. She quickly rose to become abbess, demonstrating remarkable administrative skill and spiritual leadership within the cloistered community.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Seraphina Sforza's journey from a repudiated noblewoman to a beatified abbess profoundly influenced the spiritual lives of women in Renaissance Italy and beyond. Her story provides a powerful example of resilience and devotion, leading to her formal veneration in the Catholic Church.
